claims.statement: The dependency graph is a live, timestamped, directed NetworkX multigraph of one NF application in one namespace, with node kinds network_function, service, pod, node, configmap, secret, pvc, deployment, and replicaset.
Edge kinds are calls (A depends on B, B upstream of A), runs_on (pod to node), mounts (pod to configmap/secret/pvc), managed_by (pod to replicaset/deployment), and selects (service to pod).
A workload node's health is rolled up from its managed pods: all healthy gives healthy, none healthy gives down, a mix gives degraded, and no pods or no information gives unknown.
Every node and edge carries change timestamps so the graph state at the start of a fault can be reconstructed, and graph mutation is performed only by the builders and never by the LLM.

calls edges are derived only from a grounded signal (a container's literal env var values and mounted/envFrom ConfigMap values matched against another Service name in the graph), so a missing match means no edge rather than a guessed dependency.
When cluster_enabled is False (the default), GraphBuilder.rebuild returns a built-in demo graph so the system runs without a cluster.

Cluster-free tests build the graph from a fake Kubernetes client and assert that pods, nodes, and the workload are discovered with correct node kinds and that runs_on, managed_by, and mounts edges are created.
